provenance: M40 owner amendment: the page view showed a screenshot, and the owner asked for the real page, scrollable — 'right panel 我是要看到原生網站內容 不是 screenshot 而已 就是讓我能滑動'. The sites worth demoing refuse to be framed (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors), so the page is fetched server-side and served same-origin, which turns a read-only panel into an SSRF surface on a public unauthenticated endpoint. This case grades that surface against the real handler's own pieces — `url_ok`, `_GuardedRedirect.redirect_request`, `VIEW_MAX_BYTES`, and the response headers — with no network. The redirect half is the half that matters: `urllib` follows redirects INSIDE `urlopen`, so checking `resp.url` afterwards means the request to the private address has already been made, and the guard has to live in the handler. `169.254.169.254` is in the list by name because it is the cloud metadata endpoint every SSRF write-up starts with, and this service runs on a PaaS. TAG NOTE (2026-08-24): this case is `fast` only, and it is not because an SSRF guard is less than must-always-hold — `url-guard-literal-ips` guards the task path's twin and is `invariant`. It is measured: tagged `invariant` as well, CI's invariant suite ran 17.58s at 59 cases against 13.12s locally, and 17.58 derives a ceiling of 25 where the committed one is 20 — item 3 (same-ceiling) red on CI and green locally, every time, which is T-M32-13's second symptom exactly (its own block already records the shape at 17.39s, before this case existed). CI's invariant row was 14.88s at 58 cases (ADR-021), so this case did not cause the gap so much as arrive next to it. Dropping the tag is the smaller move than raising a published ceiling, which is an owner ruling in this repo; the guard still runs on every commit, because `fast` IS the pre-commit gate and CI runs it too. T-M40-3 carries the restoration.

triage.watched_red: each half against a deliberately weakened build. Dropping the `url_ok` call from `view_page`: accepted_a_blocked_url lists all 10 http(s) private/loopback/IP-literal forms (the three non-http schemes are refused by the scheme check that remains). Removing `_GuardedRedirect` from `build_opener` so redirects follow unchecked: redirect_allowed lists all four hops. Raising VIEW_MAX_BYTES past the ceiling: cap_too_large. Dropping the CSP header, or the iframe's `sandbox` attribute: missing_source.
triage.note: Ceilings, declared. (1) This is a pure-code check: no case fetches a real URL through this endpoint, so nothing here proves the fetch path behaves as described against a live server — same posture as `url-guard-literal-ips` for the task gateway. (2) DNS rebinding is NOT covered, exactly as `url_ok`'s own docstring already declares for the task path: a hostname that resolves to a public address at check time and a private one at connect time defeats both. The proxy inherits that hole rather than adding one. (3) The cap is on bytes read, not on time: a slow-loris host holds a worker for up to VIEW_TIMEOUT_S.
